api:
<Ridgeline data={readings} value={|r: &Reading| r.temperature} group={|r: &Reading| r.month} />
PropTypeDefault
dataas aboverequired
valueFn(&T) -> f64required
groupFn(&T) -> &str: one curve per grouprequired
bandwidthf64: kernel width, in units of valueSilverman's rule, per group
overlapf64: the tallest curve's height, in rows1.6
fill_opacityf320.75
x_axisAxisConfigAxisConfig::new()
tooltip, class

Each curve is a Gaussian kernel density estimate. The first group is at the top. Lower bandwidth shows more detail; higher smooths more.

examples.title: Temperatures by month
examples.description: One density curve per month, overlapping.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn temperatures() {
    let data = use_signal(months());
    rsx! { <Ridgeline data={data} value={|m: &Measure| m.value} group={|m: &Measure| m.group} x_axis={AxisConfig::new().label("°C")} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Less overlap
examples.code:
#[component]
fn tight() {
    let data = use_signal(months());
    rsx! { <Ridgeline data={data} value={|m: &Measure| m.value} group={|m: &Measure| m.group} overlap={0.9} fill_opacity={0.9} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Wide bandwidth
examples.description: A fixed 5-unit bandwidth smooths the curves.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn smooth() {
    let data = use_signal(measures(
        &[("Small", 20., 4.), ("Medium", 35., 6.), ("Large", 55., 10.)],
        150,
    ));
    rsx! { <Ridgeline data={data} value={|m: &Measure| m.value} group={|m: &Measure| m.group} bandwidth={5.} class="h-72" /> }
}
